name: The Fort Dearborn Massacre monument (Carl Rohl-Smith, 1893), 18th Street at Calumet Avenue

grade.why: Pictured: 3 of the pictures on the Images tab show it.

documented_range.note: Placed in 1893 and moved to the Chicago Historical Society in 1931; neither the day it was set up nor the day it was taken down is read here, so the range is the two years whole. It covers the 1904 scene and neither 1812 nor 1835.

change_note: Built T-3567 (2026-11-12): the monument stands in the 1904 scene, on the new pure-Python monument archetype. Refined T-3568 (2026-11-13): the pedestal's depths read through a camera on Taylor's 1893 view (base 2.85 m, plinth 1.8, die 1.6, were 3.3, 2.3 and 1.9 reconstructed); cameras on ICHi-19208, Taylor 1893 and Detroit LC-D4-12552.

placement.position_note: The base's south-west corner. Placed by T-3568 through two cameras. EAST AND WEST, the Detroit print LC-D4-12552 (data/reference_views/pullman_house_1729_prairie/detroit_det_4a08066.json, the Pullman house's camera, its heading fitted on the house at 2.4-2.6 px rms): the pedestal's centre stands at x 800 px of the 1024 px print, a bearing of 330.4 degrees from the eye, which crosses the base's centre line (N -3198.76) at E 1501.3, 4.8 m east of T-3567's place by eye (E 1496.5). NORTH AND SOUTH, ICHi-19208 (data/reference_views/fort_dearborn_massacre_monument_1893/chm_ichi_19208.json, fitted on the pedestal alone): the estate wall's foot runs behind the monument at y 775 px, 11.8 m from the eye, 4.1 m north of the base's front, against the parcel's 18th Street line at 4.7 m (prairie_1729's south edge, N -3195.5 in data/street_grid/1904.json); so the base's centre stays 3.25 m south of that line, where T-3567 set it. Good to about 1.5 m east and west (a 10 px error in the Detroit print's bearing is 0.7 m there) and 0.6 m north and south. Two things do not agree with it yet and are open in the match records: the Detroit camera, fitted on the house 80-90 m off, does not hold its foreground and draws the pedestal at about 0.57 of the size the print shows; and through ICHi-19208 the Pullman stable's draft (pullman_house_1729_prairie_ranges) stands about 6 m east of the end the print shows at its left edge. The texts disagree on the place (the 1893 Rand, McNally guide 'at the foot of Eighteenth Street'; the 1905 Views of Chicago 'at Eighteenth Street and Prairie Avenue'; all quoted on Chicagology, no source records); the photographs are followed. Rotation 359.62 degrees squares its front to 18th Street's line (bearing 89.62 degrees); the corner also moved 0.225 m north when the base's depth went from 3.3 m to 2.85 m, so that its centre stays on the line.
placement.symbolic_location: The north walk of E. 18th Street at its east end, where it curves into Calumet Avenue: before the Pullman estate's 18th Street wall, east of the Pullman stable's end (local E 1501.3, N -3198.76 at the base's centre).

group_h_m.note: The group with its rock, over the cap: 0.3 m of rock and 2.13 m of figures to the tip of Black Partridge's standing feather. Read since T-3582 joint by joint on ICHi-19208 through its solved camera (data/reference_views/fort_dearborn_massacre_monument_1893/chm_ichi_19208.json), each joint put in depth by J. W. Taylor's 1893 camera (aic_taylor_1893.json): the feather's tip at y 130 px and the tomahawk's head at y 156 px stand 2.13 and 2.03 m over the rock's foot, the warrior's head 1.58 m. THE TWO CAMERAS DISAGREE ON THIS HEIGHT, and the record takes ICHi's: through Taylor's camera the same figures read about 10 per cent taller (every joint 25-85 px high in the print, the rock itself 25-30 px, at any depth the joint could stand at), which is about 2.35 m of figures. Taylor's camera is fitted on the base, plinth and die alone, so the group is above the last thing it holds; ICHi's is the square-on view a visitor on the walk has. The Inter Ocean's group 'about nine feet' (2.7 m, 15 September 1892, quoted on Chicagology; no source record, so a check, not a citation) and Wikipedia's 'about nine feet' (wikipedia_fort_dearborn_massacre_monument, cited for the text alone, its rights unresolved) sit nearer Taylor's reading than ICHi's if they count the rock. The figures' places and poses are the generator's (generators/archetypes/monument.py FIGURES), to about 0.15 m in depth; faces, dress folds, feathers and the group's rear are reconstructed (L-fort-dearborn-monument-3567). Was 2.75 m (T-3567), from the figures 270 px over the cap read at the die's scale and pushed back 1 m.

panels.note: A bronze panel on each face of the die: ICHi-19208 shows the front one (the column leaving the fort, in low relief) and Taylor's view the east side's; the Rand, McNally guide of 1893 (quoted on Chicagology, no source record) gives four. Their reliefs are not modelled. L-fort-dearborn-monument-3567 Since T-3589 the panels are drawn in the pale tone ICHi-19208 (c. 1900) shows them in, their relief weathered lighter than the die's granite (0.71 of white on the plate against 0.46 for the plinth's face); Taylor's 1893 print shows them fresh and dark, and the 1904 scene takes the later plate. The plate is monochrome, so the panels' green-grey is reconstructed.

lettering.value: THE FORT DEARBORN MASSACRE / AUGUST 15, 1812 / BLACK PARTRIDGE SAVING MRS. HELM
lettering.note: Cut in the die under the front panel, three lines, pale on the granite (ICHi-19208, y 667-696 px on its 1200 x 931 px copy). Built since T-3589 by generators/archetypes/monument.py (LETTER_LINES): each line centred on the die at the width and height the plate gives it, line 1 0.62 of the die's width and about 0.08 m tall, line 2 the smallest (0.11 of the width, about 0.03 m), line 3 0.37 of the width and about 0.045 m; the letters are the town's block capitals squeezed to those widths, not the cutter's face, and stand flat on the die rather than cut into it. The second line is about 4 px tall on the plate and its words are taken as the record reads them. L-fort-dearborn-monument-3567

function.note: A bronze group commissioned by George M. Pullman and placed near his house in 1893, near where the battle of 15 August 1812 was believed to have been fought.

built.note: Wikipedia: placed in 1893 'near the intersection of Prairie Avenue and 18th Street'; Chicago and Cook County Cemeteries: Pullman commissioned it in 1893 and it was removed in 1931.

research_note: THE FORT DEARBORN MASSACRE MONUMENT, built by T-3567 (piece 1 of T-3565, the owner's request of 2026-11-12 after a meeting with Bill Tyre). This record carries review_required because it depicts the battle of 15 August 1812 and Potawatomi people, in a work American Indian protesters objected to from the 1970s (karamanski_2004_monuments_lost_nation); the figures are built as the sculptor made them, as period sculpture, and the card says how the work was received. The fighting is not staged: this is the statue that stood on 18th Street, not the event. WHERE: the photographs put it at the east end of 18th Street's north walk, by the curve into Calumet Avenue, before the Pullman estate's 18th Street wall and just east of the stable's end (ICHi-19208 is captioned 'at Calumet Street and 18th' and shows the stable's rock-faced end at left; the Detroit Publishing view LC-D4-12552 shows it beyond the stable's hydrant at the curb). The texts disagree: the 1893 Rand, McNally guide has it 'at the foot of Eighteenth Street', the 1905 Views of Chicago and later accounts 'at Eighteenth Street and Prairie Avenue', a 1929 Tribune 'a few feet from Prairie avenue on 18th street' (all quoted on Chicagology, no source records); the photographs are followed. LATER: moved in 1931 to the Chicago Historical Society (chicagoandcook_2017_1812_massacre_site, wikipedia_fort_dearborn_massacre_monument), subtitled 'The Potawatomi Rescue' in 1972, protested in 1973, returned by the city to the Prairie Avenue district and later put into storage (karamanski_2004_monuments_lost_nation). Cameras on ICHi-19208, Taylor's 1893 view and the Detroit print, and the side-by-sides, are T-3568's (data/reference_views/fort_dearborn_massacre_monument_1893/): the pedestal matches them; the figures, joined from tapered limbs, do not yet read as Rohl-Smith's sculpture, and their match records say figure by figure where they differ. The Detroit print (LC-D4-12552, c. 1900) shows the lettered pedestal with no group on it: see its match record.
